UPDATE:
Even when the dishwasher was new, the rack never rolled smoothly and it easily derailed.
Customer reviews of the dishwasher warned us about this. They were correct.
I've hated the rack for years until now.

Fast forward to replacing the wheels...here's some advice that's unrelated to this specific (good) product:
As I put the new ones on, I noticed that the wheels were not aligned to each other, the issue being: the metal axles that are part of the rack are out of alignment.

So, I used a long straight edge to check the alignment of the wheels (after putting the new wheels on loosely), then I removed the wheels one at a time so I could bend (slightly) the axles on the rack. I used a small close-fitting hex socket (that just slips over the "axle") along with an extension (to get some leverage) to do the bending.

I checked the vertical alignment of the wheels and also made sure the wheels are not steering in different directions. I aligned both vertical and "toe-in" by bending the rack axles in two directions as need.

After doing this, the rack finally rolls smoothly and easily for the first time ever. Wish I had done this fix years ago!

Perfect fit. Works great, but the thermostat was not the problem. - Changed the thermostat and the fridge STILL did not work right. Frigidaire 10 cuFt top mount freezer. I live in a town with a river and people put docks on it. Years ago they would use styrofoam blocks for dock flotation; big mistake. Styrofoam has pathways between the foam cells which would allow water infiltration. Eventually the foam would become waterlogged and the docks would no longer float. Frigidaire has used this same type of styrofoam in their fridge. Where the temp sensor is mounted is a 5x3x4 inch block of foam that the temp sensor bulb snakes over and it mounted to. Also the drain tube runs through this block. BAD DESIGN. Water leaks down from the freezer and/or frost builds/melts and waterlogs this block of foam causing an ice block which affects the temperature sensor, so then the temp bulb is covered with ICE. THAT is what causes the fridge to not work properly. THE FIX: remove and replace the foam block with closed cell foam. I cut some pieces from Dow blue building foam. fridge works great now. Been running for three months perfectly. FYI: fridge was only three years old and neighbor bought a new one instead of trying to fix it! Crooked repairmen prob wanted $400 to fix!

I filled the container by slowly pouring water into the basket and letting it drain through to the mason jar until I knew that the coffee grounds were good and wet.
Then I gently poured filtered water filling up my mason jar. I set it on the counter overnight and the next morning I took the stainless steel filter out, dumped the grounds out in the garden and then rinsed it off in the kitchen sink Easy Peezy.
I saw someone mention the residue in the bottom of the mason jar, that residue is full of all of the beneficial goodness in coffee (magnesium, potassium, and various phenolic compounds, or antioxidants) and it doesn’t affect the taste or my enjoyment in the least. Actually I’m glad it’s there.
The great thing about cold brew is if you make it a little too strong for your liking it still isn’t bitter and you can easily add a little bit more filtered water to your finished coffee to tone it down a little bit.

You can adjust he amount of rinse agent to match the hardness of your water. If spotting is taking place, just bump up the release level. Use a machine cleaner each month to keep the stainless steel from developing a film! Only one design problem- if you use gelatin-based detergent pods (the soft bricks of cleaner): The detergent dispenser must be 100% clear of obstructions or the pod won't dissolve completely. No such problems with hard powder detergent capsules or gels you squeeze from a bottle into the dispensing drawer. Make sure you clean the 2 filters or you'll get redeposit problems in about a month or so. Cleaning filters is easy with an old toothbrush. Remembering to do is tougher. Freshly soiled dishes can use the 30 minute cycle and it works well- just don't put anything left out for hours on that cycle, The brief timing can't soak off dried on gook.
